answer_summary: O is 1-vinyl; P is 1-vinyl/2-azido; Q joins unit-2 CH2NH and unit-5 CH2O with an N/O methallyl bridge; R protects that nitrogen with Boc and installs CH2N3 at unit 6; S replaces N-Boc by N-Bn. Units 3 and 4, plus every otherwise unmodified primary site, retain CH2OBn, and all twelve secondary sites retain OBn.
assumptions: Problem-stated source facts: alpha-CD has six alpha-D-glucopyranoside residues; 1,2 selection is clockwise; 1,3 selection is counterclockwise; protic directing groups dominate alkenes; an NH/OH director selects the opposite unit and falls back to the 1,3 unit if the opposite site is unavailable.

Trusted general reaction laws specialized and checked as partial Lean functions: Swern oxidation followed by methylene Wittig olefination converts CH2OH to CH=CH2; alkene-directed DIBAL-H removes the selected primary O-benzyl group; MsCl/NaN3 converts CH2OH to CH2N3; DIBAL-H reduces CH2N3 to CH2NH2 while effecting the directed debenzylation; NaH with ClCH2-C(=CH2)-CH2Cl makes the N/O bridge; Boc2O and CF3COOH protect/deprotect the bridge nitrogen; NaH/BnI N-benzylates it.
Hydrogens omitted by the skeletal source drawing are represented by valence-implied attached-hydrogen counts in Lean. The azide is represented by the charge-explicit resonance form CH2-N=N(+)=N(-).
No supplementary user-model assumptions, custom axioms, official solutions, marking schemes, answer repositories, or prior competition answers are used.
